title: Lothian passes to the Scottish kings
description: After Carham, Lothian between the Forth and the Tweed is traditionally regarded as Scottish. Both the date and the significance of the battle are debated.

title: Norman conquest of England
description: William of Normandy crowned king of England. The kingdom's extent did not change, but its ruling class was largely replaced over the following decade.

title: Norman advance into Gwent
description: William fitz Osbern began Chepstow castle and pushed into Gwent, the first Norman conquest in Wales.

title: Cumbrian kingdom absorbed by Scotland (approximate)
description: The British kingdom of Strathclyde/Cumbria disappears from the record and its lands are ruled by Scottish kings. The date is a convention.

title: William II takes Carlisle
description: The Carlisle district becomes English.

title: Norman conquest of south Wales
description: After the death of Rhys ap Tewdwr (1093) Norman lords overran Brycheiniog, Glamorgan and Dyfed, founding marcher lordships.

title: Scotland gains Cumberland and Northumberland
description: David I occupied Cumberland in 1136; the Treaty of Durham (1139) granted the earldom of Northumberland to his son Henry.

title: Northern counties returned to England
description: Malcolm IV surrendered Cumberland, Westmorland and Northumberland to Henry II.

title: Scottish crown asserts control of Caithness
description: William I's campaigns brought Caithness under effective Scottish lordship; the year shown is approximate.

title: Treaty of York
description: Alexander II renounced Scottish claims to the northern English counties; the Tweed–Solway border was broadly fixed. Shown as context: the map border was already drawn on this line from 1157.

title: Treaty of Perth
description: Norway ceded the Hebrides and the Isle of Man to Scotland, keeping Orkney and Shetland.

title: Treaty of Montgomery
description: Henry III recognised Llywelyn ap Gruffudd as Prince of Wales. Llywelyn's principality was larger than the schematic zone shown.

title: Treaty of Aberconwy
description: Llywelyn confined to Gwynedd west of the Conwy; the Perfeddwlad ceded to the Crown.

title: Conquest of Wales and the Statute of Rhuddlan
description: Dafydd ap Gruffudd captured (June 1283); the Statute of Rhuddlan (1284) organised the Principality under the English Crown.

title: Treaty of Edinburgh–Northampton
description: England recognised Scottish independence under Robert I. No boundary change is shown.

title: Orkney and Shetland pledged to Scotland
description: Christian I of Denmark–Norway pledged Orkney (1468) and Shetland (1469) for his daughter Margaret's dowry; they were never redeemed.

title: Berwick finally English
description: Richard of Gloucester took Berwick, which had changed hands many times; it remained English thereafter. Too small to show as a boundary change at this scale.

title: Laws in Wales Acts
description: The Acts of 1535 and 1542 abolished the March and incorporated Wales into the kingdom of England with shires on the English model.

title: Partition of the Debatable Land
description: The Debatable Land north of Carlisle was divided along the Scots' Dike. Too small to show at this scale.

title: Union of the Crowns
description: James VI of Scotland became James I of England. The two kingdoms remained separate states with separate parliaments.

title: England declared a Commonwealth
description: Following the execution of Charles I in January 1649.

title: Scotland incorporated into the Commonwealth
description: After its conquest Scotland was incorporated by the Tender of Union (1652), confirmed by ordinance in 1654.

title: Restoration
description: Charles II restored; the separate kingdoms of England and Scotland re-established.

title: Acts of Union
description: The kingdoms of England and Scotland united as the Kingdom of Great Britain.

title: Union with Ireland
description: Creation of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland. Great Britain's boundaries are unchanged.
